quest.title: To Treat the Well-Meaning Well
quest.description: How did the samurai who lost his Vision become stuck in a quagmire of troubles brought upon him by the people?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x800, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia

talks.objective: Find the next person who lost their Vision

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They say the Tenryou Commission is directly controlled by the shogun. They're the ones responsible for maintaining law and order in Inazuma — the ones actually enforcing the Vision Hunt Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why would they take action against one of their own?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it... Huh? There seems to be some commotion over there, let's go see what's happening!

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: I'll ask one more time... Do you intend to withhold this month's emergency provisions?

dialogues.speaker: Yuuya
dialogues.text: The entire clan is counting on that food. We demand an explanation!

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: How many times do I have to say it... I don't know anything about emergency provisions.

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: You dare deceive us! Those provisions are essential, do you understand? Not some goods to be pocketed by greedy samurai!

dialogues.speaker: Yuuya
dialogues.text: You samurai think that you can just do whatever you please!? The Tenryou Commission will hear of this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Emergency provisions... like emergency food?

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: Huh? And who are you? One of Kurosawa's gang, no doubt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? We just happened to be passing by.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard the commotion and came to see what the matter was.

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: I see, you seem to have come just at the right time. Perhaps you can help us settle this matter.

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: This is Kurosawa, he's a samurai and a member of the Shogun's Army. They issue emergency provisions to the area, and he's the one responsible for distribution.

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: In the past we'd simply ask him for provisions and everything would be delivered. Now, he suddenly refuses to give us anything!

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: He's keeping the provisions for himself, I just know it! We'll starve without them!

dialogues.speaker: Yuuya
dialogues.text: No one seems to care about us... We used to think Kurosawa was a kind man, but he's shown his true colors. He's the same as all the other samurai.

dialogues.speaker: Yuuya
dialogues.text: It's no wonder all the Visions have been confiscated. The Raiden Shogun doesn't need people like him helping her rule the nation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This must be one of the people Ayaka asked us to help. But why would she ever want us to help someone like him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we should talk to Kurosawa and see what he has to say.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: I've never even heard of these emergency provisions!

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: I don't know whether it's rumors or whether they're trying to blackmail me, but either way it's ridiculous. If I was hoarding supplies, would I still be the poor man I am today?

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: My own family can barely get by as it is... Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got other matters to attend to.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We heard that you lost your Vision recently.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: That's the first bit of truth I've heard all day. The Shogun's Army told me that I was unworthy of my Vision — they said I was slacking off in my work. Apparently I'd even disappointed the Raiden Shogun. That's why they confiscated my Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well that's strange, you were helping enforce the Vision Hunt Decree. Why would you be unworthy of your Vision?

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: To be perfectly honest... I don't seem to remember the details.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: All I know is that I would perform certain things every month, but I don't recall what they were.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: And it's not just that... I have this unsettling feeling like... like someone owes me something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does it have to do with the missing emergency provisions?

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: I didn't take any! Like I said, if I was taking them for myself, I wouldn't be going through such hard times right now.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: To top it all off, my house was just raided by Treasure Hoarders... which is why I came here in the first place. I was chasing after them when I got held up by these two.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: If you don't believe me, go find the Treasure Hoarders yourself! If there were any emergency provisions to be had, they would've found them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... He seems to be telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we'd better confirm. Let's go round up those Treasure Hoarders and see what they have to say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should be able to follow their tracks. They couldn't have gone too far.

talks.objective: Go and stop the Treasure Hoarders from looting Kurosawa's house

dialogues.speaker: Ken
dialogues.text: We really outdid ourselves this time!

dialogues.speaker: Ken
dialogues.text: All those samurai houses packed with goods, haha! We really hit the jackpot. I mean, besides that one house...

dialogues.speaker: Tadao
dialogues.text: You haven't seen anything yet, there'll be a lot more where this came from!

dialogues.speaker: Tadao
dialogues.text: Today's just the beginning. I'll be leading you all on an epic journey of pillage and plunder that will go down in hoarder history!

dialogues.speaker: Gou
dialogues.text: You da man, boss!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These seem like the Treasure Hoarders we're after. Let's teach 'em a lesson!

dialogues.speaker: Ken
dialogues.text: Ugh, there goes all the Mora... We worked hard to steal that, ya know!

dialogues.speaker: Ken
dialogues.text: C'mon boss, think of something!

dialogues.speaker: Tadao
dialogues.text: Ahem... Not bad, kid... Y—You ever think of joining the Treasure Hoarders? We could use someone like you.

choices.text: Forget it. Tell us all you know about Kurosawa.

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: Kurosawa? Oh... I remember.

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: So he's the one who sent you after us, huh? Tsk, just our luck... I knew we shouldn't have hit that place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what did you see inside? Was it stuffed with food supplies?

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: Food supplies? You kidding? That place was a complete mess... All we found was a strange-looking box, hopefully with valuables inside.

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: I didn't want anyone else to see it, so I was planning on opening it myself once we got back.

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: But now that you've caught us, how about we make a deal? That little box for our freedom... Whaddya say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've got a deal. Now show us what's in the box!

response.speaker: Ken
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: What the!?

response.speaker: Gou
response.text: Th—There's nothing in here but IOUs!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, a lot of them, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And they all seem to be made out to the owner of a general goods store, a Miss Aoi... We're talking tons of Mora here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'd better go talk to this Miss Aoi and get to the bottom of this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As for you guys, you're free to go. Just pray that our paths don't cross again!

response.speaker: Ken
response.text: Y—Yes, of course!

response.speaker: Gou
response.text: So we redeemed ourselves for some IOUs... does that mean we broke even?

response.speaker: Tadao
response.text: Shut it! Let's just get out of here!

choices.text: Not likely. Word has it you looted Kurosawa's house.

talks.objective: Talk to Aoi in the general goods shop and find out what happened

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Welcome to Tsukumomono Groceries, we've got everything you need. Can I help you find something?

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Or perhaps... there's something you want to inquire about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About these IOUs...

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're friends of Kurosawa, I take it? Haha. Perhaps you're here to pay off his debts?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, let's not get ahead of ourselves... We're just here to learn where they all came from.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did Kurosawa end up owing you so much money? Did he buy anything super-expensive here?

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Kurosawa would come regularly to purchase large quantities of foodstuffs. He'd always put the payment on his own account.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: However, the price of provisions began to skyrocket recently, and his salary was no longer enough to cover the cost. So, he started writing out IOUs to cover whatever he couldn't afford of the usual amount.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's how he was getting those emergency provisions...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why did he have to purchase a "usual" amount? If the prices increased, couldn't he just buy less?

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Well if you think about it, the citizens receiving the emergency provisions must have been carefully calculating how much they needed to sustain them each time.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Kurosawa thought that it would be quite the disappointment for them if they found they didn't have enough. Especially after such long and careful planning.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: So he deemed it necessary to take on the debt rather than let the people down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Kurosawa was purchasing all the emergency provisions at his own expense...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...and no one ever appreciated what he did... They just complained and held him accountable...

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: People's attitudes will always reflect their circumstances. In the face of hardship, nobody cares to think twice.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: If you ask me, had Kurosawa told everyone the truth about the supplies from the start, then there wouldn't be such a severe backlash now.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Of course, I'm sure there would still have been some unrest. What he was doing was truly a thankless deed.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: As for why he chose to spend his own money on emergency provisions and never tell anyone... I'm still not too clear myself.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: If you're still curious, why don't you go ask him yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, he doesn't remember.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: I see... That reminds me... it seems that his Vision was recently confiscated.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Most unfortunate... If he doesn't clear the debt on his name, he'll have no choice but to sell that sword that is so dear to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sword? What sword?

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Didn't he tell you? He possesses a very valuable blade... He's carried it for years now.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: I've asked him about its origins — he told me that it was a gift from his father... that it was too precious to sell.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: In hindsight, I regret that I never made an offer on it... Everything has its price, at least that's what I think.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Why don't you ask him about the sword yourself? Perhaps it'll even provide you with the answers you are looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Oh, but before you go, if you would kindly settle today's bill...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But we didn't buy anything!

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Hehe, information is also a kind of commodity, wouldn't you agree?

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I won't charge much for information about Kurosawa. Nothing we ever discussed was explicitly confidential anyway. Let me think... 2,000 Mora should be a fair price.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fair enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: At least we now know where the emergency provisions were coming from, plus we found out that Kurosawa has a priceless sword in his possession.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go talk to Kurosawa again and see if he can remember anything...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm, what are you doing here all by yourself? Where did those other two go?

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: I presented them with a choice: either they left or I drew my sword. They left.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: It turned out to be a real time-saver, actually. Perhaps I should start using it more often...

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: Did you manage to track down the Treasure Hoarders? Everything I said was true, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That just about sums it up. It turns out that you really were distributing emergency provisions, but they were all purchased at your own expense.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: Strange... Is that really the kind of person I was?

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: I don't really have any such recollection. Even after all you've told me, I still don't remember anything.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: Why was I purchasing emergency provisions for everyone? And why would I put myself in such a difficult situation... *sigh* I really don't understand.

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: But I cannot deny that when I brandished my sword to scare those two away, I could sense that my body was somehow reluctant to do so.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: This sword was once wielded by my father.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: I remember once when I was young, I wanted to sneak out with the blade and show it off to the kids next door. My father ended up catching me in the act and scolded me severely.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: What did he say... Huh. I can't seem to remember that either.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: It would seem that I forgot many important things when my Vision was taken from me. So many memories, gone forever, no matter how hard I try to remember.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: All I can remember now is my father telling me that this blade bore his life's creed. Before he passed away, he placed the sword in my hands...

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: ...and said to me, "With this sword, you should—"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey... If you look carefully, there seems to be some words engraved on the hilt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you recognize the words?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The words are: "Virtue and Justice."

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: "Virtue and Justice"?

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: Somehow, those two words seem to explain everything now...

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: Taking on seemingly endless debts to make others happy. I guess that must have been my greatest ambition after all...

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: But what use are virtue and justice? I purchased the provisions for those in need, and look how things ended up.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: The Tenryou Commission seized my Vision, and the very people I was so desperately trying to help, refuse to understand me.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: And the irony of all of it is... I somehow still felt sorry when threatening them with my blade.

response.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
response.text: I'm incapable of being a good person... yet I'm equally unable to be bad. I—I don't know what to do with myself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yet another troubled soul...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When we get the chance, let's speak to Thoma about Kurosawa's debt. The Yashiro Commission would surely help cover his expenses.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In any case, we must never let him sell off that sword.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, seems like losing all ambition is a terrible experience.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fortunately for us, you don't have a Vision.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go find the next poor soul.

choices.text: Mind if we have a look?

dialogues.speaker: Yuuya
dialogues.text: The emergency provisions... what will we do without them?

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: A person without a conscience is a person without honor!

dialogues.speaker: Oomori
dialogues.text: Enough lies — cough up the provisions!

dialogues.speaker: Yuuya
dialogues.text: *whimpering* How will we ever get by without those provisions...

dialogues.speaker: Kurosawa Kyounosuke
dialogues.text: I never thought that one day I'd be relying on Treasure Hoarders to prove my innocence.
